A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the behavior of banks is shaped not only by their own characteristics but by the characteristics of the markets in which they operate.

we have provided a better understanding of the behavior of banks in the unsecured and secured interbank funds markets, and of the effects of bank risk taking and liquidity shocks on the efficiency of the financial system.

the interaction of banks across different markets is a key factor in the functioning of financial markets and in the transmission of liquidity shocks, and that the regulation of banks in the different markets can affect their behavior and performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
banks interact across different financial markets in order to mitigate their exposure to risk, to diversify their funding, and to obtain liquidity.

banks can benefit from interacting with different financial markets, but they need to manage carefully their risk exposures and their liquidity positions in order to avoid the potential adverse effects of these interactions.
banks can benefit from diversification and alternative funding sources, but this can make them more vulnerable and expose them to contagion risk.
